summary: The Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP), funded by the Government of Japan, pays for mid-career development professionals from developing countries to do a master's at a listed participating programme abroad. It covers tuition, a monthly living stipend, economy travel with a travel allowance, and basic health insurance. Winners usually have at least three years of paid development work, a full-time development job now, and an unconditional admission letter already in hand.
lookfor: At least 3 years of paid, development-related work after your bachelor's, and a full-time development job now
Unconditional admission (except for funding) to a participating master's programme outside your home country
Two strong professional recommendations from people who supervised your work
A clear statement of purpose linking your work, the programme and your country's development
A complete, eligible application — strict rules (e.g. exactly two recommendations) are enforced
cycle: 2027 study: Window 1 runs 18 Jan – 26 Feb 2027 (results for finalists likely by end of March 2027); Window 2 runs 29 Mar – 21 May 2027 (12:00 noon EST). Each window covers a different list of participating programmes. You must hold an unconditional admission letter before you apply, so university applications must be done months earlier.

eligibility.q: Are you a national of a developing World Bank member country listed in the guidelines, with no dual citizenship of a developed country?
eligibility.no: Check Annex 1 of the guidelines. If your country is not listed, this award is closed to you.

eligibility.q: Did you earn your bachelor's degree at least 3 years before the application deadline?
eligibility.no: Wait until you meet the 3-year gap, and build development work experience meanwhile.

eligibility.q: Do you have at least 3 years of paid, development-related employment, gained within the last 6 years and after your bachelor's?
eligibility.no: Keep working in a development-related job. Unpaid volunteering generally does not count (special rules apply to fragile/conflict-affected states). Check whether NYSC counts in the FAQ before relying on it.

eligibility.q: Are you employed full-time in development-related work now?
eligibility.no: You must be in a full-time development job when you submit. Consider awards without this rule (e.g. Chevening or Commonwealth Scholarships).

eligibility.q: Will you hold an unconditional (except for financing) admission letter to a participating programme outside your country of citizenship and residence by the window deadline?
eligibility.no: Apply to the programme first. If you cannot get admission in time for Window 1, aim for Window 2 programmes or the next year.

eligibility.q: Are you not a World Bank Group employee or a close relative of one?
eligibility.no: WBG staff and close relatives are not eligible.

steps.title: Confirm you are eligible
steps.why: JJ/WBGSP rejects ineligible applications without review. Work-experience rules are the most common problem.
do: Open the World Bank Scholarships page and download the 2027 Application Guidelines and FAQ for developing country nationals (Window 1 and Window 2).
Check your country is in Annex 1 and you have no developed-country dual citizenship.
Count your paid development-related work since your bachelor's, month by month, within the last 6 years. You need at least 3 years.
Count part-time work at its percentage (e.g. 50% for half-time), as the FAQ asks you to state.
Confirm you are employed full-time in development work now.
tips: The FAQ lists many development fields (agriculture, health, education, infrastructure, finance, environment). Map your jobs to them.
avoid: Counting student jobs, internships or unpaid volunteering as paid development work.
check: I have a month-by-month count showing 3+ years of qualifying work.

steps.title: Pick your window and participating programmes
steps.why: Only listed participating programmes qualify, and each window has its own list. Dual degrees with a participating programme are not accepted.
do: Open the participating programmes page, then the Window 1 and Window 2 lists.
Window 1 (18 Jan – 26 Feb 2027) includes programmes such as Columbia SIPA's MPA in Economic Policy Management, Brandeis Heller, Johns Hopkins MPH and Yale.

Window 2 (29 Mar – 21 May 2027) includes programmes such as IHE Delft water programmes, ANU climate/environment masters, Leeds, Tokyo agricultural development and Saitama civil and environmental engineering.
Choose 2–4 programmes in your field, located outside your country of citizenship and residence.
Note each programme's own admission deadline — usually well before the JJ/WBGSP window.
tips: If you are late for Window 1 admissions, Window 2 programmes give you extra months.
avoid: Applying to a non-listed programme at a listed university.
check: I have a ranked list of participating programmes and their admission deadlines.

steps.title: Build your timeline backwards
steps.why: You need admission before you can apply, so the real work starts 6–9 months before the window.
do: Write each programme's admission deadline (often October–January) in your calendar.
Add JJ/WBGSP dates: Window 1 opens 18 Jan, closes 26 Feb 2027; Window 2 opens 29 Mar, closes 21 May 2027.
Set targets: English test and transcripts done 3 months before the first admission deadline; recommenders asked 2 months before the JJ/WBGSP window.
Plan to submit at least one week before the window closes, as the guidelines advise.
tips: Ask programmes whether they can issue admission decisions in time for your window.
avoid: Thinking you can apply to JJ/WBGSP first and to the university later.
check: Admission and JJ/WBGSP dates are in my calendar.

steps.title: Apply for admission and get an unconditional offer
steps.why: No application is reviewed without proof of unconditional admission (except for financing and/or medical certificate).
do: Apply to your chosen programmes through each university's portal.
Upload transcripts, degree certificate, CV, statement and references as each university asks.
Meet any conditions (e.g. English score) quickly so the offer becomes unconditional.
Download the admission letter as a PDF once received.
tips: Tell the programme you are applying for JJ/WBGSP; many are used to this timeline.
avoid: Uploading a conditional offer — it makes the application ineligible.
check: I have an unconditional (except financing) admission letter.

steps.title: Book your English test early
steps.why: JJ/WBGSP does not set its own English test, but your programme's admission usually does.
do: Check each programme's English requirement.
Book IELTS/TOEFL (in Nigeria, IELTS centres in Lagos, Abuja and other cities; check the fee in naira on the booking site).
Send scores to the universities as instructed.
tips: Ask if an English-medium degree letter is accepted to save cost.
avoid: Taking the test too late for the admission deadline.
check: My English score meets every programme's requirement.

steps.title: Prepare your CV on the official template
steps.why: The CV must use the template in Annex 4 of the guidelines and shows your qualifying work experience.
do: Open Annex 4 in the Application Guidelines.
Fill in each job with exact start/end dates, employer, title, duties and whether full- or part-time (with % time for part-time).
Highlight how each job is development-related.
Write in English (or the programme's language where allowed).
tips: Use results with numbers: farmers trained, km of road, budgets managed.
avoid: Using your own CV format instead of the template.
check: My CV follows Annex 4 and dates add up to 3+ years.

steps.title: Collect employment proof and diplomas
steps.why: You must document the 3-year paid work requirement and upload your degree diplomas.
do: Ask each employer (or HR) for a letter on letterhead with your title, dates, full-time/part-time status and duties.
Gather other proof if letters are hard to get (contracts, payslips) — check what the guidelines accept.
Scan your bachelor's diploma (and any advanced degree diploma).
Check your passport is valid; finalists must send a passport scan within 3 business days of an offer.
tips: Ask for employment letters early — HR offices can be slow.
avoid: Letters without dates or employment type.
check: Proof covers every month I count toward 3 years.

steps.title: Write your statement of purpose
steps.why: The application form includes a Statement of Purpose section. It is where you show the development impact of your study.
do: Open the form when the window opens and copy the exact questions and limits.
Explain the development problem you work on, using one concrete example from your job.
Show what you have achieved in your 3+ years of development work.
Explain why this programme, naming courses or skills you need.
Describe how you will apply the degree in your country after graduation.
tips: Write for a busy reviewer: clear headings, short paragraphs, numbers.
avoid: Generic statements about 'poverty in Africa' without your own role.
check: My statement links my work, the programme and my country's development.

steps.prompt: Statement of Purpose: your development work, why this programme, and how you will contribute to your country's development.
steps.limit: Check the current guidance (shown in the application form)

steps.title: Plan your career section
steps.why: Reviewers look for a credible plan to use the degree in development work.
do: Write a 5-year plan: the role, the organisation type, the problem you will tackle.
Link it to your current job and to a specific skill from the programme.
Use this plan in the statement of purpose and with your recommenders.
avoid: Saying you plan to stay abroad permanently — the programme aims to build capacity at home.
check: I can state my post-degree plan in three sentences.
steps.prompt: Your career goals after the master's.

steps.title: Get exactly two professional recommendations
steps.why: You need exactly two recommendations; one is not enough and three or more disqualifies you. They must come from people who know your paid work.
do: Choose two current or former supervisors who saw your development work recently.
Do not use professors who only know you from coursework.
In the application system, submit the Recommendation Request Form; each recommender gets a system email.
Send them your CV and statement so they can write specifics.
Check both are received before the deadline.
tips: Submit the request form as soon as the window opens to give recommenders time.
avoid: Asking a third person 'just in case' — it disqualifies you.

steps.title: Complete and submit the online application
steps.why: Incomplete applications are not reviewed. The guidelines advise submitting at least one week early.
do: Open the online application from the World Bank Scholarships page when your window opens.
Complete: employment and employment history, residence, Statement of Purpose, signature page.
Upload: admission letter, CV (Annex 4), diplomas, employment proof.
Check dates in the form match the CV and letters.
Submit and save the confirmation.
tips: Fill the form offline first, then paste.
avoid: Mismatched dates between CV and employment letters.
check: I have a submission confirmation and both recommendations are in.

steps.title: Respond fast if you are a finalist
steps.why: Window 1 finalists hear by about the end of March 2027. Offers have tight follow-up deadlines.
do: Check your email daily after the deadline.
Send your passport scan within 3 business days of an offer.
Get a medical certificate (less than 3 months old) confirming you are fit to travel and study.
Accept the offer as instructed.
tips: Keep your passport scan ready on your phone.
check: I have accepted and sent all finalist documents.

steps.title: Get your visa and plan your finances
steps.why: The scholarship does not pay visa costs, family support or enrolment deposits.
do: Apply for your student visa (US programmes require a J-1 visa).
Budget for visa fees, any university deposit and initial costs.
Arrange leave or resignation with your employer.
Plan travel with the university and the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat.
tips: Save money for the first weeks before the stipend arrives.
avoid: Assuming the scholarship covers family members.
check: Visa is in process and I have funds for uncovered costs.

faq.q: Can I apply before I get admission?
faq.a: No. You need an unconditional (except for financing) admission letter to a participating programme when you apply.
Yes, if it is paid and development-related; state the percentage of time worked in your CV.
No. Exactly two; three or more disqualifies the application.
Tuition, a monthly living stipend, economy travel with a travel allowance, and basic health insurance. Not visa costs, family support or deposits.

faq.q: Can I study in my own country?
faq.a: No. The programme must be outside your country of citizenship and residence.
